records.literal_gloss: A psalm for thanksgiving. Shout to YHWH, all the earth.

en.L: A psalm for thanksgiving. \q Shout for joy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all the earth.
en.B: A psalm for giving thanks. \q Raise a glad shout to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all the earth!
en.R: A song for giving thanks. \q Everyone on earth, shout to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with joy!

decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.
The word (todah) is thanks, and also the thank offering (Leviticus 7:12). The psalm may have been sung when such an offering was brought; verse 4 has worshipers entering the temple gates with thanks.

decisions.choice: shout: the cry that greets a king
decisions.reason: The same verb (heria') as 98:4 and 95:1: the glad shout raised for the King.

source.text: עִבְד֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה בְּשִׂמְחָ֑ה בֹּ֥אוּ לְ֝פָנָ֗יו בִּרְנָנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Serve YHWH with gladness; come before him with a joyful cry.

en.L: Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with gladness; \q come before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with joyful singing.
en.B: Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and be glad doing it; \q come before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with ringing cries of joy.
en.R: Be happy as you serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} singing for joy!

decisions.reason: The verb ('avad) is the work a servant does for a master or subjects for a king, and also worship (Exodus 3:12). All the earth is called to serve the LORD as King.

decisions.choice: a joyful cry: a ringing shout or song
decisions.reason: The word (renanah) is a loud cry of joy.

source.text: דְּע֗וּ כִּֽי־יְהוָה֮ ה֤וּא אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים הֽוּא־עָ֭שָׂנוּ וְל֣וֹ אֲנַ֑חְנוּ עַ֝מּ֗וֹ וְצֹ֣אן מַרְעִיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Know that YHWH, he [is] God; he made us, and his [are] we, his people and [the] flock of his pasture.

en.L: Know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] God! \q It [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [who] made us, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} [are] we, \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and the flock of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} pasture.
en.B: Be sure of this: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is God! \q He is the one who made us, and we belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q We are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, the flock {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pastures.
en.R: You must understand that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is the true God. \q He made us, and we belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q We are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. We are like sheep, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cares for us like a shepherd.

decisions.choice: and we are his: the words as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes "and not (lo') we" and its notes say to read "and his (lo) we [are]"; the two sound alike. The written form gives "he made us, and not we ourselves", which the ancient Greek translation follows. The form to be read fits the next words, "his people and the flock of his pasture", and the words here follow it.
To know here is to recognize and confess (46:11), not only to have heard.

decisions.choice: the flock of his pasture: the people he shepherds
decisions.reason: As in 95:7 and 79:13, God's people are his flock and he is their shepherd.
Readable brings out the emphasis of "the LORD, he is God" (1 Kings 18:39).

decisions.choice: like sheep, and he cares for us like a shepherd
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison (m3).

source.text: בֹּ֤אוּ שְׁעָרָ֨יו׀בְּתוֹדָ֗ה חֲצֵרֹתָ֥יו בִּתְהִלָּ֑ה הֽוֹדוּ־ל֝֗וֹ בָּרֲכ֥וּ שְׁמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Enter his gates with thanksgiving, his courts with praise; give thanks to him, bless his name.

en.L: Enter {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} gates with thanksgiving, \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} courts with praise; \q give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, bless {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.B: Come through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} gates giving thanks, \q into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} courtyards with praise; \q thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and bless {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: Go through the gates of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple thanking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q Go into its courtyards praising {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q Thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and praise {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

decisions.choice: gates and courts: the way into the temple
decisions.reason: Worshipers went in through the temple gates into its open courts (24:7; 96:8).

decisions.choice: thanksgiving: thanks, perhaps a thank offering
decisions.reason: The word (todah) is the same as in the title (verse 1).
Readable says whose gates these are.

source.text: כִּי־ט֣וֹב יְ֭הֹוָה לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְעַד־דֹּ֥ר וָ֝דֹ֗ר אֱמוּנָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For good [is] YHWH; forever [is] his loyal love, and to generation and generation his faithfulness.

en.L: For good [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; forever [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love, \q and to generation and generation {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithfulness.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is good; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love has no end, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithfulness stands from one generation to the next.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is good! His faithful love lasts forever. \q He keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promises to every generation, one after another.

decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: the song of the temple: good, love forever
decisions.reason: "Good" and "his loyal love is forever" are the words of the temple's great song of thanks (106:1; 107:1; 118:1; 136:1; 2 Chronicles 5:13).
The word ('emunah) is steadiness, being someone others can rely on.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.
Readable says what God's faithfulness does.
